To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effects of substituting amino acids for casein on calorie and nitrogen gains are dependent on the age of the rat and the level of calorie and nitrogen intake.
the effects of dietary nitrogen source on nitrogen storage in the rat are influenced by the level of energy intake and by the age of the animal.

(1) at low levels of energy intake, the amino acid mixture was as effective as casein in supporting nitrogen gains in young rats, and (2) at low levels both of energy and nitrogen intake, the amino-acid mixture was as effective in supporting nitrogen gains as casein in adult rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of varying the source and the quantity of nitrogen and the quantity of calories on the storage of calories and nitrogen in rats of 28 and 100 days of ages.
the effects of varying nitrogen and/or calorie intake on nitrogen and/or calorie storage in rats.
the effect of the source of nitrogen on nitrogen and calorie storage by young and adult rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, at the levels of calorie and nitrogen intake used, the substitution of a mixture of amino acid for casein resulted in a significant difference in nitrogen gains only for the adult animals at the higher level of nitrogen intake, and in no significant difference in calorie storage.
nitrogen gains were greater for rats receiving case-in than for rats receiving amino acids, but calorie storage was unaffected by the type of nitrogen source fed.
the amino acid mixture was as good as the purified casein in promoting nitrogen storage, and that the amino acid source was not a limiting factor in the storage of calories.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, at low nitrogen intake, the amino acid mixture is as effective as casein in promoting growth, but, at higher nitrogen intake, casein is superior to the amino acid mixture.
the effects of nitrogen source on nitrogen storage are more pronounced in young than in adult rats and that the effects are more marked at higher than at lower nitrogen intakes.
, for young rats, nitrogen storage was not influenced by the source of nitrogen, but for adult rats, nitrogen storage depended on the source of nitrogen.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amino acid mixture is not equivalent to casein in terms of its effects on nitrogen retention.
the amino acid profile of the nitrogen source is important for nitrogen storage, but that the energy source does not affect the amount of nitrogen stored.
the amino acid mixture is an adequate replacement for casein, but that it is important to take into consideration the animal’s physiological status when making the substitution.
